easy.explanation: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done.
easy.q: To whom did Ahab tell all that Elijah had done?

easy.explanation: Jezebel threatened to make Elijah's life like the life of one of the prophets he had slain.
easy.q: What did Jezebel threaten to do to Elijah?

easy.explanation: Elijah came to Beersheba, which belonged to Judah.
easy.q: Where did Elijah go after he fled?

answers: He was discouraged and asked to die
He was sent to find Elisha
medium.explanation: Elijah went into the wilderness, sat under a juniper tree, and requested that he might die.
medium.q: Why did Elijah continue from Beersheba into the wilderness?

answers: He fled to save his life
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Elijah fleeing because of Jezebel's threat.
medium.q: What does the phrase “went for his life” mean in context?

answers: He went into the wilderness, came to Beersheba, and fled from Jezebel
He came to Beersheba, went into the wilderness, and asked to die
He asked to die, told Jezebel, and came to Beersheba
medium.explanation: Elijah came to Beersheba, left his servant there, went into the wilderness, and asked to die.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes Elijah's actions?

answers: Elijah continued alone into the wilderness
Elijah appointed the servant as a prophet
The servant went to Jezebel in his place
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Elijah left his servant there and continued by himself.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Elijah leaving his servant at Beersheba?

answers: Elijah, who had acted boldly before, became discouraged and asked to die
Jezebel fled while Ahab pursued her
The servant became a leader and Elijah became his servant
challenge.explanation: Despite his earlier deeds, Elijah is now described as discouraged because of the threat.
challenge.q: What striking contrast is described in these verses?

answers: A lack of water in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Jezebel sent him a threatening message, after which Elijah fled.
challenge.q: What directly caused Elijah to flee?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Angel and Food on the Journey to Horeb
paragraphs.title: The Angel and Food on the Journey to Horeb

easy.explanation: An angel touched Elijah and told him to arise and eat.
easy.q: Who awakened Elijah under the juniper tree?

answers: A cake baked on the coals and a cruse of water
Fruit and a vessel of oil
easy.explanation: Elijah saw a cake baked on the coals and a cruse of water.
easy.q: What did Elijah see at his head?

easy.explanation: Elijah went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb.
easy.q: How long did Elijah travel to the mount of God?

medium.explanation: The angel came to Elijah a second time and told him to arise and eat.
medium.q: How many times did the angel provide Elijah with food and water?

answers: The journey is long and difficult for you
medium.explanation: The angel told Elijah to eat because the journey ahead was too great for him without strength.
medium.q: What does “the journey is too great for thee” mean?

answers: So he could return to Beersheba
So he would have strength for the long journey
So he could speak with Ahab
medium.explanation: The angel said that the journey was too great, so Elijah needed food and strength.
medium.q: Why did the angel tell Elijah to eat again?

answers: The food enabled him to make the long journey to Horeb
The food caused him to remain under the juniper tree
The food was intended for the servant left at Beersheba
challenge.explanation: The passage connects his eating with traveling forty days and forty nights.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the food Elijah received and what happened next?

answers: The first meal was not enough for the journey
Elijah refused to leave for Horeb
The angel wanted him to return to Jezebel
challenge.explanation: After eating the first time, Elijah lay down again, so the angel awakened him and told him to eat again.
challenge.q: What does the angel's return a second time suggest?

challenge.explanation: Elijah went unto Horeb, the mount of God.
challenge.q: What was Elijah's destination after the journey?

paragraphs.idea: The Angel and Food on the Journey to Horeb

paragraphs.paragraph: The Revelation at Horeb and the Still Small Voice
paragraphs.title: The Revelation at Horeb and the Still Small Voice

easy.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Elijah and asked, “What doest thou here, Elijah?”
easy.q: What did the LORD ask Elijah in the cave?

answers: That he had been jealous for the LORD and was left alone
That he wanted to be king
easy.explanation: Elijah said that Israel had forsaken God's covenant, that the prophets had been slain, and that he alone was left.
easy.q: What did Elijah claim in his answer?

easy.explanation: After the fire came a still small voice.

medium.explanation: After the wind came an earthquake, and after the earthquake came fire.
medium.q: What came after the great and strong wind?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the quiet voice that came after the wind, earthquake, and fire.
medium.q: What does “a still small voice” describe in these verses?

answers: He wrapped his face in his mantle
medium.explanation: Elijah wrapped his face in his mantle and went out to the entrance of the cave.
medium.q: How did Elijah respond when he heard the still small voice?

answers: The revelation is associated with the still small voice rather than the violent phenomena
The wind and earthquake are more important than the voice
The fire caused Elijah to leave Horeb
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the LORD was not in the wind, earthquake, or fire; afterward came the still small voice.
challenge.q: What does the sequence of wind, earthquake, and fire emphasize in contrast with the still small voice?

answers: He still felt zealous and alone
He had already found all the prophets
He no longer cared about Israel
challenge.explanation: Elijah repeats that Israel had forsaken the covenant, the prophets had been slain, and he was left alone.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Elijah repeating his answer about his condition?

answers: Wind, earthquake, fire, still small voice
Still small voice, fire, earthquake, wind
challenge.explanation: The verses describe a great wind, an earthquake, a fire, and then a still small voice.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the events at Horeb?

paragraphs.idea: The Revelation at Horeb and the Still Small Voice

paragraphs.paragraph: New Missions and the Remnant of Israel
paragraphs.title: New Missions and the Remnant of Israel

easy.explanation: The LORD told Elijah to anoint Hazael to be king over Syria.
easy.q: Whom was Elijah told to anoint as king over Syria?

easy.explanation: Jehu was to be anointed king over Israel.
easy.q: Over whom was Jehu to be anointed king?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel.”
easy.q: How many faithful people had the LORD left in Israel?

answers: To be prophet in Elijah's room
To be captain of Jehu's army
medium.explanation: Elisha was to be anointed to be prophet in Elijah's room.
medium.q: What role was appointed for Elisha?

answers: The one who escapes being killed by the sword
The one who holds the sword
The one who searches for a sword
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to someone who escapes the sword but will later be judged by another appointed leader.
medium.q: What does “him that escapeth the sword” mean?

answers: They were appointed to carry out future judgment and leadership
They were all members of Elijah's family
They all traveled with Elijah into the wilderness
medium.explanation: The LORD assigned Elijah to appoint them and explained their future roles.
medium.q: What relationship did Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha have according to the LORD's word?

answers: His claim did not reflect the whole situation in Israel
challenge.explanation: The LORD revealed that seven thousand had not bowed unto Baal or kissed him.
challenge.q: What does the information about the seven thousand faithful people show about Elijah's claim that he was left alone?

challenge.explanation: The LORD first mentioned Hazael, then Jehu, and finally Elisha.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of the appointments given to Elijah?

answers: Faithfulness involved both refusing to worship Baal and avoiding acts of allegiance to him
challenge.explanation: The verse describes their faithfulness through two things they had not done: bowing to Baal and kissing him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from describing the faithful as those who had not bowed unto Baal or kissed him?

paragraphs.idea: New Missions and the Remnant of Israel

paragraphs.paragraph: The Appointment of Elisha as Prophet
paragraphs.title: The Appointment of Elisha as Prophet

answers: Plowing with twelve yoke of oxen
easy.explanation: Elisha was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen, and he was with the twelfth.
easy.q: What was Elisha doing when Elijah found him?

easy.explanation: Elijah passed by Elisha and cast his mantle upon him.
easy.q: What did Elijah cast upon Elisha?

easy.explanation: Elisha asked permission to kiss his father and mother before following Elijah.
easy.q: What did Elisha ask to do before following Elijah?

answers: He slew the oxen, prepared the meat, and gave it to the people
medium.explanation: Elisha took a yoke of oxen, slew them, boiled their flesh, and gave it to the people.
medium.q: What did Elisha do after saying farewell to his parents?

answers: A pair or team of animals
medium.explanation: A yoke refers to a pair or team of oxen used together for plowing.
medium.q: What does “yoke” mean in the phrase “twelve yoke of oxen”?

answers: To leave his former life and provide food for the people
To hide the oxen in the wilderness
medium.explanation: He left his former work, used the oxen for a sacrifice and feast, and gave the food to the people.
medium.q: Why did Elisha slay the oxen and boil their flesh?

answers: He decided to follow Elijah and serve him
He wanted to remain only a farmer
challenge.explanation: After leaving his former life, Elisha went after Elijah and ministered unto him.
challenge.q: What does Elisha's action show about his decision?

answers: Elijah left Elisha free to choose and decide
Elijah commanded Elisha to become king
Elijah announced that the calling was canceled
challenge.explanation: Elijah's response did not force Elisha; Elisha demonstrated his decision through his actions.
challenge.q: What may be understood from Elijah's reply, “Go back again: for what have I done to thee?”

answers: He changed from a plowman to Elijah's servant
He changed from a king to a prophet
He changed from an angel to a man
challenge.explanation: At first Elisha was plowing, but by the end he followed Elijah and ministered unto him.
challenge.q: What change took place in Elisha by the end of the passage?

paragraphs.idea: The Appointment of Elisha as Prophet
